intro: おろか means "foolish": A はおろか says it would be foolish even to bring A up, so you skip it and go straight to B. A is the obvious case, B is the extreme one, and the whole sentence carries the speaker's surprise or dismay. English "let alone" works, but in Japanese the obvious case comes first.

skills.rule: A はおろか B も / さえ / まで: let alone A, even B; A is the obvious case, B the extreme one.
skills.explain:
はおろか follows a noun, or a verb in the dictionary form plus こと: 漢字はおろか, 走ることはおろか. The second half takes も, さえ or まで on B. Both halves are true: in 漢字はおろか、ひらがなも書けない he cannot write kanji, and cannot even write hiragana.

Order is the opposite of English. Japanese says the obvious case first: the harder thing in a negative sentence, the bigger or nearer thing in a positive one. It is mostly used for negative or alarming situations, but an impressive positive fact also works: 国内はおろか海外でも有名だ.

はおろか is emotional and descriptive. The second half cannot be a request, an invitation or your own plan. For "of course A, and B too, please", use はもちろん. If A turns out false ("far from A"), it is どころか, not はおろか.
patterns: [obvious case] はおろか、[extreme case] も / さえ [negative]
[verb] ことはおろか、[verb] こともできない
[smaller place] はおろか [bigger place] でも [positive]

examples.jp: 漢字[かんじ]{はおろか}、ひらがなも書[か]けない。
examples.en: I can't even write hiragana, let alone kanji.

examples.jp: 祖父[そふ]はスマホ{はおろか}、パソコンも使[つか]ったことがない。
examples.en: My grandfather has never even used a computer, let alone a smartphone.

examples.jp: 足[あし]をけがして、走[はし]ること{はおろか}、歩[ある]くこともできない。
examples.en: I've hurt my leg and can't even walk, let alone run.

examples.jp: 忙[いそが]しくて、旅行[りょこう]{はおろか}、週末[しゅうまつ]に休[やす]むこともできない。
examples.en: I'm so busy I can't even rest at the weekend, let alone take a trip.

examples.jp: 彼[かれ]は貯金[ちょきん]{はおろか}、今月[こんげつ]の家賃[やちん]さえ払[はら]えない。
examples.en: He can't even pay this month's rent, let alone save money.

examples.jp: その作家[さっか]の名前[なまえ]は、国内[こくない]{はおろか}海外[かいがい]でも知[し]られている。
examples.en: That writer's name is known not just in Japan but abroad as well.

contrast.note: はもちろん is neutral and can end in a request: 名前はもちろん住所も書いてください. はおろか is emotional and cannot.
どころか can deny A: 痩せるどころか太った (far from losing weight, I gained). With はおろか, A is never denied; both halves hold.
ばかりか adds a surprising B to A in a neutral reporting tone. はおろか dismisses A as not even worth mentioning.

mistakes.bad: ひらがな{はおろか}、漢字[かんじ]も書[か]けない。
mistakes.good: 漢字[かんじ]{はおろか}、ひらがなも書[か]けない。
mistakes.note: In a negative sentence the harder thing comes first and the easier thing goes with も.

mistakes.bad: 名前[なまえ]{はおろか}、住所[じゅうしょ]も書[か]いてください。
mistakes.good: 名前[なまえ]はもちろん、住所[じゅうしょ]も書[か]いてください。
mistakes.note: はおろか cannot lead into a request; use はもちろん.

skills.tip: Read A with a dismissive "never mind A": if B is even more extreme and both are true, it is はおろか.
